text:
🇻🇳There's a Vietnam template that everyone has been following lately. HCMC, Hanoi, Da Nang and Phu Quoc. 

And no, I’m not saying skip them. Please go.
But also, don’t stop there?!
 
Here are just a few places in Vietnam worth going to next time you visit: 

1. Ha Giang —
Dramatic mountain passes, winding roads, and some of the most surreal landscapes in Southeast Asia.
Not for comfort seekers. Which is exactly why it’s fun. 

2. Ninh Binh —
The larger world does it like a day trip from Hanoi. I urge you to stay there for 2 days at least.  

3. Phong Nha —
Was, is, and will always be my Vietnam. Fell in love with the spot 11 years ago, and have returned back for every visit. 

4. Quy Nhon —
Underrated coastline, clear waters, away from the tourist traps.  A nice spot if you are seeking that 'live like a local' energy. 

5. Da Lat —
Cool weather, pine forests, aesthetic cafés just a cosy spot to chill at, away from the big cities. 

6. Con Dao —
Raw, quiet, and far less commercialised. Slightly eerie if you know its history. Beaches here feel untouched and away from the tourists radar for now. 

I’ve done all of these except Con Dao.
That’s next on my list unless something else distracts me (very likely).

Which one would you add to your Vietnam Trip? 
And if you’ve found a spot that surprised you, I want to know.

text:
I traveled to Asia for the first time, and spent 1 month in Vietnam, Da Nang 🌏🇻🇳

Here's my honest feedback of this trip 👇

People

Probably the first thing I noticed, before traffic or anything else, was how people greet you (except for the airport, because it looked a bit scary at passport control with all the red warning signs lol).
Vietnamese people are incredibly nice, kind, and smiling most of the time. It feels like they're just truly happy and want to share that with you.

Food

I don't think there was even one time in a month when we went somewhere and we did not like it.
Food is incredible!
Perhaps Pho Bo wasn't my favorite, the traditional one, but overall, Da Nang offered great food experiences. Vietnamese, Asian overall, European cuisine, everything tasted really good.
I have so many places saved on the map!

Prices

We rented a decent apartment in an expat neighborhood in Da Nang, and it cost around $500/month.
You can easily eat on $10 (for 2!).
As a woman, I kept up my beauty routine, and I was surprised how affordable it is to look good in Vietnam (nails, laser, beautician, etc.).
I even had my first hospital experience there (just for a checkup). It went well and was super cheap compared to Europe.

Traffic and pollution

I cannot forget about these two things, as it was a bit wild for me, especially for the first few days.
Even when leaving Vietnam, I was still scared to cross the road as I used to. Pretty much nobody stops, and if you don't learn how to 'go with the flow' and just let bikes/scooters pass you, you're cooked, my friend :)

The air was also pretty polluted most of the time. Once I even didn't feel well because of that and the heat combined (when we wanted to watch fireworks in Da Nang).

Even the fact that the city is by the sea didn't help much.
Also, in many areas the city looked really dirty (I just wish the government did something about that, because the nature is beautiful, people are amazing, and it would look so much better if it was clean and neat).

Hoi An, for example, was more peaceful, with less pollution and traffic.

Next time I would rather stay there and go to Da Nang if I really needed to (a taxi from Da Nang to Hoi An was around $11-13, so it's really affordable for such a distance).

Digital nomad experience overall

Vietnam seems like a great place for digital nomads, with a huge variety of coffee places, coworking spaces, and things to do.

Plus, I'm so happy we visited famous Ba Na Hills and the Golden Bridge, the French Village.
Yes, we paid $100, which is expensive for Vietnam, but it was a WOW-pass, and it was totally worth it!

If I had to lock in there for some time, that'd be possible even despite some downsides.

Overall, it was a great experience, and I'm happy to be able to explore Asia for the first time.

Now I'm in Chiang Mai, Thailand 🇹🇭, and I'll be happy to share these experiences with you as well! 

Let me know if you have any questions in the comments below, and follow my digital nomad journey 🫶

text:
Da Nang Hotels FAQ: Beach, Budget, and Booking

Quick answers on where to stay in Da Nang, cheap hotels, family resorts, and how early to book My Khe Beach hotels.

Where should I stay in Da Nang?
My Khe if you want the beach outside. Han River if you want food and the Dragon Bridge. Non Nuoc if you want a quieter family resort.
Are cheap hotels in Da Nang worth it?
Yes, if recent reviews are clean and the pin is near An Thuong, My Khe, or the river. Skip the lowest price on the edge of town.

How early should I book?
For Tet and June–August, book several weeks ahead. Beach weekends and festival nights fill first. Outside those peaks, a flexible rate a few days out is often enough.
Is the Dragon Bridge near the beach hotels?
No. It is a city-center show, usually Saturday and Sunday evening. Stay on the Han River if that night is the point of the trip. Stay on My Khe if the morning swim matters more.

Can I day-trip to Hoi An?
Yes. That is the simplest plan: one Da Nang hotel, one unpack, Hoi An as a day out.

Here’s exactly how I’d spend 48 hours in Hue + what everything costs 🧵 1/11

text:
Da Nang is a beach city with a mountain day built in.

Best feel:

Feb–May: drier, clearer beach days
Jun–Aug: hotter, more sudden rain
Sep–Nov: more typhoon risk — watch forecasts
Dec–Jan: cooler, good for walking Son Tra and Marble Mountains
Crowd hacks: Ba Na Hills on a weekday before 8 am. My Khe at sunrise. Dragon Bridge show only Fri–Sun around 9 pm, so build the night around that.

Keywords: best time to visit Da Nang, Da Nang weather, Da Nang travel tips, avoid crowds Ba Na Hills, Da Nang rainy season

Da Nang has been an absolute BLAST!!🇻🇳

Honestly I am a big city guy and came here mainly because indie hackers on X were raving about it, and I wanted a quieter place to launch my app.

But it has become one of my favorite place I have ever been to!

> super chill and beautiful
> everything is close, great beach 10min away
> insane density of beautiful cafes to work from, great coworking spaces 
> amazing food and coffee
> awesome community, lots of indie hackers and nomads - met so many great people here 
> very cheap - I spent around 1600$ per month (but also lived in a good hotel and was going to restaurants every day)

If you are considering coming here - you should! I’ll definitely be back soon!

text:
When to Book Da Nang Hotels: Peak, Value, and Rain
Tet and summer are the expensive windows for hotels in Da Nang. See when My Khe rates spike and when a flexible booking is the better deal.

Da Nang hotel prices do not follow one season. Tet, around late January to mid-February, is a hard spike. June to August is the domestic beach peak, and weekend occupancy in the city can run very high. September to November is wetter and usually cheaper. February to May, outside Tet, is often the better mix of weather and price.

Book early if your dates hit Tet, a summer weekend, or a fireworks festival on the river. Book flexible if you are traveling in the shoulder. A free-cancellation rate lets you recheck a week out without losing the room.

Beachfront My Khe and river hotels near an event fill before generic city rooms. If the dates are fixed, take the area you want first and the exact room second.

text:
Ba Na Hills from Da Nang: Where to Stay for an Easy Day Trip

Planning Ba Na Hills from Da Nang? Pick a hotel that makes the early start simple, then compare My Khe and city-center stays.

Ba Na Hills is a day trip, not a second hotel. The Golden Bridge and the hill station sit above the city, so the useful base is a Da Nang room you can leave early and return to at night.

My Khe works if you want the beach after the hills. A Han River hotel is easier if you care more about dinner than a sunrise swim. Either way, unpack once. Book a flexible rate: hill weather and cable-car queues both move the plan.

Leave after breakfast, go early on a weekday, and keep the evening free. A beach hotel with a pool is the better recovery than a resort an hour from the pickup point.

text:
Left Da Nang and will probably not come back. 

Spent a total of 5 weeks here. 

I went to bed slightly angry almost every night because of bad service/hospitality, noise, dangerous driving or a mix of those. 

It affected my gf even more so we decided to not stay longer than 1 month.

I think that’s a good proxy for liking a place. Our nervous system just never really felt at ease.

In terms of Vietnam in general, I feel like I had a much better time in HCMC when I stayed there for two weeks a few years ago. 

Everything seemed to be more efficient there and people were much friendlier.

All my Vietnamese friends are super cool, funny and really friendly. 

So I was quite disappointed when I noticed most locals in Da Nang being so cold and borderline unfriendly.

This is the first city in South East Asia this happened to me and if anyone knows why I’d love to learn more about it. 

Maybe it was just us? Maybe locals just don’t like tourists/foreigners? 

No idea but it felt “off”. Almost not welcomed.

The Indiehacker community is really cool and friendly though.

Some cafes are definitely nice to work from Da Nang and the actual coffee is great. Just strong… very strong hehe

The thing with those coffee shops is just that I’m slowly approaching 30 and can’t sit on ultra uncomfortable chairs for an entire day anymore (👴)

When I first arrived I was super stoked because there are not a lot of nomad spots with breezy sunny weather in Jan/Feb and Da Nang definitely has that.

The cons unfortunately outweigh the pros so I’ll likely not come back for the foreseeable future. 

All that being said, if you have a short runway and want to save money it might still be one of the better places to go so I’d say it’s worth giving it a try!

quoted_tweet.text:
Arrived in Da Nang! 🇻🇳 

I think we arrived with too high expectations 😬 

It honestly feels like Bali but ordered on Wish but in a good way… let me explain.

So after three days here my pros and cons:

Pros:

- ☀️ Amazing weather early in the year

(not too cold not too hot, way better than Bali/BKK/CNX. Think T-Shirt during the day but light wind jacket at night.)

- 💸 Affordable 

(you def. feel it’s much cheaper than most „Nomad“ places but it does come with a cost I‘ll share below)

- 👨🏽‍💻 Community 

(there’s a lot of cool Indiehackers here and you’ll def never feel alone)

- ☕️ Coffee shops 

(this came to a surprise! I’d dare to say the the work-from-a-cafe culture here is the best I have seen from all the places I have been too. Big, spacious, natural light, great coffee, decent WiFi and power plags everywhere)

Now to the cons:

- 🏠 Accommodation 

(this is a personal one but I just can’t seem to find a nice looking apartment or house here for short term rental.

Da Nang seems amazing if you are conscious about your run rate and want basic amenities (think 200-500$ for a basic one bedroom condo)

But if you are used to accommodation from Bali or Bangkok it just doesn’t deliver. 

A good amount of places seem to be riddled with either mold or noise issues. 

We’ve been on countless visits today with various agents, checked all the booking sites and… nada.

There seems to be some nicer high end stuff but it’s all not possible to rent on a monthly basis and seems to avg. $2-4000/m which suddenly doesn’t seem appealing at all anymore given the other options in SEA and beyond.

This is actually also the most frustrating and likely what won’t keep us here for long. 

Still scouting but my initial optimism to find something decent is fading fast.

- Driving style 🛵

(I’m sorry to say this but after having driven a lot of vehicles around South East Asia, Vietnam seems to have the worst drivers of all countries I have ever been to with India coming close second)

Initially I thought „oh nice people drive quite slowly here most of time like 40km/h max and there’s no traffic“ so it was refreshing to the traffic craze of Bali but fuak me do people here drive dangerously!

People not only drive on the wrong side of the street (typical SEA behaviour I can handle) but they corner you with acceleration on the wrong side of the street 😅🤯 It’s absolutely nuts. 

We almost had a horrific accident today. My girlfriend cried because it was so sketchy.)

So ye… to summarize Da Nang seems to be THE place if you are starting out your Indiehacker journey and/or want to save money. 

If you care a lot about the quality of your accom or plan to ride a bike while having little to no experience I’m not sure it’s the best place to go.

I think Da Nang didn’t start out or ever want to be a nomad hub but it’s slowly turning into it so maybe it’s also not fair to compare it with a place like Bali.

I’m writing this because I really want Da Nang to work for us (given the pros I mentioned) but it seems like a rough start. 

I’ll update y’all in a few weeks with how it’s going 😉

text:
today is my last day in da nang, vietnam 🇻🇳

here are a few things i learned while being here:

– insane good local food + drink for about $2-3

– the city is right at the ocean which gives it a really special vibe

– rent a scooter (~$50/month), there are so many beautiful places to ride to around here and the freedom it gives you is just on another level

– the area around da nang is stunning, some of the most beautiful scenery i've seen

– right now there are a lot of people here from X, perfect place to meet a ton of new and interesting people

– many cozy coffee shops you can work from

– so many people here right now that chances are high you'll run into someone you know at a random café

– the center is super compact, just small streets everywhere and you can walk to basically everything. perfect for coffee shop hopping and grabbing food in between

– you can walk around at any time of day or night and never feel unsafe

– the locals are incredibly friendly. english is often not spoken that well but it's never a problem to communicate (and honestly that's totally fine, i'm in their country so i should be the one learning their language, can't complain if they don't speak english when i don't speak vietnamese)

– if you rent a scooter watch out for the police, they pull you over and ask for a lot of money. don't pay more than $10 (they wanted $200 from me)

– often went on late night walks on the beach which has a really special vibe

– this is the place if you're trying to go all in and not making money yet. you can live here on $600-800 a month (probably the bare minimum budget but still)

da nang is for me the best place i've been so far to try and build a living with my apps: super cheap, right at the ocean, made some great friends here, and so many people with the same goal :)

text:
I’ve started to believe much more in designing your environment around the life you want.

My four months in Da Nang made that obvious. I was more productive, less stressed, and generally had more energy to work on things.

A lot of it came down to simple things. Living near the sea. Having sports like pickleball easy to join. Eating healthy food without spending much. Working from good coffee shops surrounded by other people working and building things. Almost never spending more than 15 minutes getting somewhere.

There’s also something about being around people doing similar things. You exchange ideas, learn from each other, and naturally get more motivated. Even things like sauna, cold plunge, yoga, sound healing, or art therapy are accessible enough to become part of normal life instead of something you do once in a while.

I’ve spent time in Seoul, Fukuoka, Frankfurt, Tokyo, Melbourne, Taipei, Hong Kong and other cities over the past couple of years, and you can build a similar lifestyle in many places.

The difference is that in a lot of cities, it gets expensive very quickly. A comfortable short-term apartment, sports, good food, cafés, wellness, and living close to everything can easily add up to a few thousand dollars a month.

That’s what makes Da Nang feel special to me. It’s not that it has something no other city has. It’s that a really good daily life is unusually easy to build there.

That’s what makes Da Nang feel special to me. It’s not that it has something no other city has. It’s that a really good daily life is unusually easy to build there.

text:
five days in da nang and here’s my honest take so far:

first thing i noticed → the airport is ridiculously close to the beach.
like 15–20 minutes and you’re at an international airport. for digital nomads or frequent travelers this is honestly heaven.

second → the buildings are kinda adorable.
super narrow, tall, almost like stacked apartments. usually just a few units per building. it gives the city a very unique look.

third → baguettes.
i knew the history, but i did not expect baguettes to be everywhere and actually good.
you order steak? baguette on the side.
random meal? baguette appears.
not complaining.

food prices surprised me in a good way.
if you don’t like cooking and you have a decent income, you can easily eat western food for like $3–7 per meal. pizza, steak, burgers, western breakfast, all super tasty.

the beach is wide and really nice.
i get why some people call it the miami of asia. it also feels more modern than i expected.

something i didn’t expect → random karaoke everywhere.
small restaurants, tiny bars, street spots.
people just sing. dance. vibe.
and there are fireworks at night which makes the whole city feel weirdly festive all the time.

crossing the street is a skill you unlock here.
zebra crossing means nothing.
you just walk slowly and confidently and let the bikes flow around you. survival mode but it works.

one downside → massages are more expensive than thailand and bali.
and i lowkey wish there were more coffee shops directly on the beach because working with ocean view is my favorite.

weather right now is also nice.
around 25° which feels way easier than 30 in malaysia last week.

overall → da nang feels easy to live in.
good food, good prices, modern enough, beach life, fast airport access.

still early review, but so far… i get the hype.

I just left 🇻🇳 Da Nang Beach 🇻🇳
Unpopular opinion: I will not go back. 

What is good 👍

🍜 Affordable food
💻 Startup scene, laptops everywhere
🏗️ Feels like China 20 years ago, strong development vibes.
🏙️ Da Nang city (15 min taxi from the beach) has very  good infrastructure in terms of food, gyms, cafes. Way better than the beach area.

What is not good 👎
💸 Rents doubled recent years. We paid $600 for 21 days Airbnb. Construction noise from 5 AM, no hot water, ants
🚧 Construction IS everywhere. The architectural landscape honestly looks like a mess
🐀 Broken streets, trash, food waste, holes, rats everywhere
🪼 The ocean is only good if you enjoy swimming with jellyfish

My verdict 🗺️
If your budget is tight and you want a developer community, Da Nang is your launchpad. Especially for long-term stays where you can negotiate lower rent. Just decide early: beach or city apartment. Do your homework first.
- Otherwise, I would stay away.

#DaNang #Vietnam #Travel #DigitalNomad

text:
Let me share my views

An Indian tourist planning a trip will wanna cover the country with the following  cities which fall in a straight line. 

Ho Chi Minh + Phu Quoc (Optional) > Da Nang + Hoi An > Hanoi + Halong Bay

In this too Phu Quoc will be covered by some tourists

Ho Chi Minh also many tourists skip as it's a business capital etc with limited attractions. Just for them Da Nang made sense but then most of them wanna cover Ho Chi Minh also so they done with the country at one go and don't have to come back. Unlike Thailand etc where there are repeat travellers Vietnam would have less. I maybe wrong against  the data if any but just my thoughts.

Flying into Da Nang would not work for most as it's right in the middle of Ho Chi Minh and Hanoi which doesn't go well with covering the other places in the later part of the trip. If not planning to fly across all cities but go via land it's all the more cumbersome. 

Da Nang made sense for those who wanted to skip Goa costs and run to some beach location but then Thailand has so many such options + it's Visa Free so tourists would also prefer to take a small getaway to Thailand than Vietnam. 

Vietnam picked up immensely as they were the first to open up and start off tourism without complicated rules and regulations. And not kept changing the same every few weeks like how Thailand was doing. Confusing rules and regulations and kept changing every few months etc.

text:
🌎 Nomad destinations in order of popularity now! 

I have to admit, the number of nomads, expats, and immigrants coming to Paraguay and deciding to stay permanently is growing fast. Especially over the past few years.

Paraguay is definitely more expensive than Da Nang when it comes to food, rent, and general living. And Da Nang has the beach. I love that town/hoi ann, and that whole area of Vietnam. That is probably why more nomads end up here. Because they are usually building business, not setup yet! 

But land and real estate prices in VN are like Sydney, London, New York prices. You cannot own land as a foreigner. You cannot get residency. You cannot get a great steak every day at a good price. And the capital gains tax or tax on foreign sourced income is around 20%, if they even bother paying it. I wanted to live there several years ago. No.1 on my list. PY was always No.3-4 on my list. I am so glad I chose PY in the end. Saved a lot of time and mucking around!

Paraguay is the perfect home base, safe haven, tax haven. You are legal. You can own land. You can live free. And then you just travel and spend time in these other fun, adventuroues countries.

text:
Big cities are logistically easier, and people often default to them. But there’s so much more to Vietnam than just these 3 cities. And honestly, connectivity isn’t a problem. Vietnamese are so resourceful! Someone will always patch you up with some form of transport to get just about anywhere. 

The last client I planned a trip for, they stayed in Ninh Binh for 2 nights - such a refreshing change from the usual day trip. Also props to them for trusting me on it, and miss Da Nang.

Seating is quite comfortable and there are plenty of power outlets.

Food options are plenty

There's comfortable AC inside.

Easy to get to via Grab.

There's background music but it does not get very loud. 

Still, headphones needed for any real work.

text:
had an amazing month in vietnam, da nang.  

it reminded me of the sense of presence and alignment i felt during my first few months living in bali in 2022, when everything just felt right.

i’ve been in asia for almost 5 years and for some reason never took the step to try vietnam, with the preconceived idea that it was too underdeveloped to properly grow my trading and that the simplicity of life would feel too limiting.

turns out it became one of my favorite countries in asia.

da nang area has pretty much everything:

- airport 15 min by taxi from the city center
- top-tier food and restaurants from pretty much every cuisine
- literally eating a high-quality, protein-focused diet for barely $10–15 a meal
- tons of options and the ability to book hotels the same day without any pressure at affordable prices
- top-tier flexibility and freedom
- clean roads overall, beautiful long beaches to walk around, and a more natural, untouched peninsula
- beautiful preserved nature and rice fields just 30 min away by bike (hoi an)
- plenty of outdoor calisthenics parks and spaces to train
- a city that breathes health and happiness, where elderly people are exercising everywhere from early morning until sunset (the health of its elderly population tells you absolutely everything you need to know about a city)

i’ve lived roughly 3 years in indonesia, 1 year in thailand, 1 year in japan, and visited pretty much every other major destination in asia.

so far, da nang might be one of the best combinations i’ve found for anyone looking for peace, calm, quality of life, great value, and a beautiful setup close to the ocean.

flying to chiang mai, thailand this week for the first time. 

got a bunch of friends to see and hoping to meet some new people while i’m there.

feel free to comment if you live in chiang mai or have any recommendations 🙏🏼

i’ve been in asia for almost 5 years and for some reason never took the step to try vietnam, with the preconceived idea that it was too underdeveloped to properly grow my trading and that the simplicity of life would feel too limiting.

turns out it became one of my favorite countries in asia.

da nang area has pretty much everything:

- airport 15 min by taxi from the city center
- top-tier food and restaurants from pretty much every cuisine
- literally eating a high-quality, protein-focused diet for barely $10–15 a meal
- tons of options and the ability to book hotels the same day without any pressure at affordable prices
- top-tier flexibility and freedom
- clean roads overall, beautiful long beaches to walk around, and a more natural, untouched peninsula
- beautiful preserved nature and rice fields just 30 min away by bike (hoi an)
- plenty of outdoor calisthenics parks and spaces to train
- a city that breathes health and happiness, where elderly people are exercising everywhere from early morning until sunset (the health of its elderly population tells you absolutely everything you need to know about a city)

i’ve lived roughly 3 years in indonesia, 1 year in thailand, 1 year in japan, and visited pretty much every other major destination in asia.

so far, da nang might be one of the best combinations i’ve found for anyone looking for peace, calm, quality of life, great value, and a beautiful setup close to the ocean.

flying to chiang mai, thailand this week for the first time. 

got a bunch of friends to see and hoping to meet some new people while i’m there.

feel free to comment if you live in chiang mai or have any recommendations 🙏🏼

text:
gm gm

one month in vietnam today. here are a few things i learned:

-you can eat a proper meal for $1–$2. and i don’t mean snacks. actual food.

-da nang is LOUD. constant traffic, constant beeping, a banh bao guy driving around with a speaker all day, and a garbage truck that plays a melody at 5-6am that woke me up more times than i’d like to admit.

-hoi an surprised me the most. slower, calmer, more nature. i ended up liking it much more than da nang.

-crossing the street is an experience. it honestly feels like cars and bikes here don’t come with brakes. at first it feels impossible. eventually you learn the trick: walk slowly and let the traffic flow around you.

-grab bike rides might be my favorite thing here. for $0.50–$1 someone will drive you 15–20 minutes across the city.
-people are kind and many speak basic english, which made things easier than i expected.

these are just a few observations after my first month here. i’m writing a full guide about my experience and tips for vietnam soon.

So a few things:

I think the uncomfortable truth is that many of the immigrants that come to Portugal (and rest of Southern Europe) particularly South Asia work really hard, many work harder than Portuguese because they have more at stake

Majority of the Uber drivers are South Asian, their cars are generally cleaner and they're much friendlier than the very frustrated, stressed and angry native Portuguese Uber drivers (who are probably angry cause they getting squeezed out of the market by immigrants to be fair)

99% of the South Asians in Portugal I talked to are very honest about their game plan:
- Stay in Portugal 5 years then get the passport
- They work hard, in farming, factories as Uber driver
- Often their wife also works, but they don't register as a couple. Why? Well....
- A large share of them often work illegally (as in unregistered), while registering as unemployed and apply for free welfare benefits which are very easy to get in Portugal, this is 100% welfare fraud
- A lot of the money (both work + welfare) is sent back to families in their home countries, some of the money is invested in real estate at home or in places like Dubai
- Once they get their Portuguese passport after 5 years, they get instant access to the European Union, can live anywhere and they say they will move to UK or Germany, for better work opportunities (and possibly welfare too)

You have to understand one thing, to us this feels like dishonest fraud and it absolutely is but to them they're just hacking the system without considering much about the long term damage

One thing I learnt is the South Asians I met were all very friendly to me and they're just trying to get themselves out of poverty, you gotta imagine what you would do in their situ

What we have to do in Europe is completely shutdown welfare for new immigrants first 10-20 years or so or at least until you've paid net into the system enough

text:
Working from Homnay Cafe in Da Nang 🇻🇳 today

All in all a decent place in Da Nang to work from.

Seating is fine with good chairs upstaris in the co-working section.

Quite good for short and long sessions.

Power outlets are att he walll, where seating is less comfortable.

Internet is FAST at 296.90 Mbps down and 222.22 mbps up. 

Prices are elevated for Da Nang, a salted coffee is VND 59k ($2.18)

AC is very comfy here.

Power outlets are plenty around the walls. This place was made to ship.

Easy to get to via Grab.

You can ship at any time from here from 7:00 am to 10:00 pm

They have a decent menu with plenty of food options

They play light background music, but the place can get noisy inside with people talking.

Headphones and a white noise app are recommend to lock in.

text:
Detailed breakdown of my monthly living expenses in Vietnam's 3 biggest cities    

III. Da Nang - top 1 city for tourism
- $260 rent a 1 bedroom (incl. utilities)  
- $250 for food (avg $1-2/meal; eating out 2-3 times/week runs about $10-15 each)  
- $60 for amazing coffee (in Vietnam, coffee shops basically double as coworking spaces, so you can save on office costs with just a $1.5-2 coffee) 
- $150 for various expenses (entertainments, insurance etc)  
- $50 tools, internet, phone  
- $50 for transportation (if you own a motorbike, this cost is only $10)

Total: $780/month

Da Nang highlights:
1. Nature & scenery
- My Khe Beach: long, clean beach with sunrise views
- Marble Mountains: caves, temples & panoramic city views
- Son Tra Peninsula: jungle, monkeys & the Lady Buddha statue
- Hai Van Pass: one of the most beautiful coastal drives in Asia

2. Food you must try
- Mì Quảng: signature Da Nang noodles
- Bún chả cá & bánh canh seafood noodles
- Fresh seafood by the beach (cheap & high quality)
- Vietnamese coffee & local night street snacks

3. Local experiences
- Dragon Bridge fire & water show (weekend nights)
- Sunset beach walks & early morning ocean swims
- Café hopping with ocean views
- Day trips to Hoi An ancient town & Ba Na Hills

- $50 tools, internet, phone 
- $50 for transportation (if you own a motorbike, this cost is only $10)  

Total: $1185/month  

HCM City highlights:
1. Culture & history
- Independence Palace: historic site marking the end of the Vietnam War
- War Remnants Museum: powerful and eye opening war history
- Notre Dame Cathedral & Central Post Office: French colonial icons
- Chinatown Saigon (Chợ Lớn) & Thien Hau Temple: rich Chinese Vietnamese heritage

2. Food you must try
- Bánh mì & cơm tấm (broken rice with grilled pork)
- Bún bò & hủ tiếu street noodles
- Vietnamese drip coffee & salt coffee
- Street food in District 1 & District 4 (cheap and insanely good)

text:
🇻🇳 THE SMARTEST WAY TO TRAVEL CENTRAL VIETNAM IN 2026

Planning Da Nang, Hoi An and Hue?

One of the biggest mistakes first-time visitors make is changing hotels every night just to be closer to the next attraction.

There is an easier way.

📍 Use Da Nang as your main base.

Da Nang gives you easy access to the airport, My Khe Beach, restaurants and some of Central Vietnam’s most popular destinations.

A practical first trip can look like this:

DAY 1 — DA NANG
Arrive, check in and keep the first day easy.

Explore My Khe Beach, the Han River, Dragon Bridge, local food or simply recover after your flight.

Avoid putting an expensive full-day attraction immediately after arrival — flight, immigration and luggage delays can easily change your schedule.

DAY 2 — BA NA HILLS & GOLDEN BRIDGE
Give Ba Na Hills its own day.

Mountain weather can be very different from the weather in Da Nang city, so check conditions again close to departure.

DAY 3 — HOI AN
There is no need to move hotels just for one night.

A very practical route is:

Da Nang → Cam Thanh Coconut Forest → Hoi An Ancient Town → sunset → dinner → lanterns → return to Da Nang.

Hoi An becomes especially beautiful from late afternoon into the evening.

DAY 4 — HUE
If history and Vietnamese culture are important to you, give Hue a full day.

A comfortable route from Da Nang can include:

Da Nang → Hai Van Pass → Lang Co → Hue Imperial City → Royal Tombs → Thien Mu Pagoda → Da Nang.

Hue should not be treated as a quick photo stop.

DAY 5 — KEEP ONE FLEXIBLE DAY
This is one of the most useful things you can do in Central Vietnam.

Use it for:

• Marble Mountains
• Son Tra Peninsula
• local food
• shopping
• massage & spa
• beach time
• a private Da Nang city experience
• Cham Island when sea conditions are suitable

🌧️ IMPORTANT WEATHER TIP

Do not build your entire Central Vietnam itinerary around a weather forecast checked weeks in advance.

Da Nang city, Ba Na Hills, Hue and the sea can have very different conditions on the same day.

Marine activities are especially dependent on wind, waves and local operating conditions — not only rain.

A flexible itinerary is often much more valuable than trying to visit every famous attraction.

✈️ DEPARTURE DAY TIP

Keep your final day light.

Coffee, shopping, beach, massage or a short city visit are much safer choices than putting Hue, Ba Na Hills or another long-distance trip immediately before your flight.

The goal is not to see the greatest number of places.

The goal is to spend less time packing, waiting and travelling — and more time actually experiencing Central Vietnam.

text:
in 2 days i'm moving to Vietnam 🇻🇳 to start over and try to make it online

it's been one of my biggest dreams for years. to make enough money online to travel around Asia like a nomad, without worrying about next month

it started in 2022 with @levelsio's blog. i was reading it at work, about how he packed everything into a backpack and moved to Asia

"that's so cool!" i thought, as i kept binging his articles

but after that i just went back to my 9-5 job :D

for 4 years it stayed a "one day" thing

then a few months ago my feed filled up with people who moved to Da Nang and said it changed their life

they weren't famous founders making millions or anything like that, just normal people building stuff online like me

so i thought, if they can do it, why can't i?

i don't make enough online yet, at least not as much as i need

but i know i work best with my back against the wall. when i burn the bridges and making it is the only option left, i HAVE TO find a way

we'll see if it works this time too

i'll keep building mobile apps, keep growing my social app and keep building in public

i have enough money saved for about 4-5 months

by then, i need to make at least $1k/mo in profit to keep living my dream

i have a rough plan for it and i'll write about the whole thing here every day

i expected to be scared, but i'm not, and i don't really know why/how

it's the biggest decision of my life and i feel no anxiety at all

just excited, like something big is about to change

that has to be a good sign, right?

anywaay if you live in Da Nang (or did), pls tell me any tips & tricks you have

coffee's on me when i get there!

text:
Han River Hotels in Da Nang: City Stays Near the Dragon Bridge 
Looking for Han River hotels in Da Nang? See why the city center beats the beach for food and nightlife, what to check before you book, and where to compare live rates.

Stay on the Han River if the beach is a bonus, not the whole trip. City-center hotels in Da Nang put you next to the Dragon Bridge, night markets, and local restaurants. My Khe is a short Grab ride, usually 10–20 minutes, not a walk.

Why do we expect America to tolerate it?

text:
Our SaaS just crossed $13,500 in the last month!

This is how this came to be:

After dropping out one year ago from our CS degree in Spain and having created 3 failed projects in 8 months, my cofounder @PabloSantanaT and I, started working on a new SaaS, RankInPublic. 

We tried to ship it as quick as possible, we did it in single 16 hour sprint, from idea to MVP.

At the time the situation with my family wasn't very good, my parentsrecently divorced and, I was starting to get pressured into going back to university, to finish a degree to work at a 9-5 for the rest of my life...

I really felt like a loser.

But then one day I saw two posts, one by @levelsio talking about how if he were broke again he would move to Vietnam and lock in, and another by @tdinh_me talking about how they were building the @HackerResidency in Da Nang (Vietnam).

This seemed like the perfect opportunity. I took my life time savings, $4k, and I booked a one way ticket and a hotel for $190 a month in Da Nang, Vietnam.

Once there I had the chance to meet a lot of incredible people, people that taught us a lot, people who inspired us to push to higher limits. 

One day, after two months of working on RankInPublic we got our first payment. Someone wanted to sponsor the tournament!!! That day was one of the happiest days of my life :)

Since then we have been working hard on RankInPublic, every single day.

And now, after 7 months in, and after a few weeks of stagnation and questioning if everything was over, suddenly we started making $1k+ per day.

We didn't change a single line of code, but we discovered how to market the product.

We had set a goal of $10k a month for our SaaS, and now after achieving the goal in less than two weeks, we are doubling down and setting a new goal, $100k a month.

I don't know how much time it will take us, but I know we will achieve it.

text:
As a Vietnamese person, I think I can add a bit of context to this.

Your experience in Da Nang is actually something I’ve heard from some foreigners before.

HCMC and Da Nang are very different cities.

HCMC has a lot of international companies and expats, so people there are more used to foreigners and English is more common.

It’s also known for having the best service culture in Vietnam.

But the downside is obvious:
traffic, noise, and air quality are worse because it’s a fast-growing megacity.

Da Nang is almost the opposite.
Pros:
- beautiful city
- great beach and sunshine
- much better air quality
- cheaper cost of living

But the trade-offs are:

- smaller city
- fewer English speakers
- service culture not as strong as HCMC
- fewer expat-heavy neighborhoods

In HCMC you have areas like Thao Dien, District 1, District 7 where locals interact with foreigners every day, and many foreigners live and work there long-term.

Da Nang is much smaller, and foreigners are more spread out, so locals may feel more reserved, not necessarily unfriendly.

Ah, one more thing I personally love about HCMC:
It’s basically a city that never sleeps.

You can find 24/7 cafes where people are coding, building startups, studying, or working late at night.
There are also 24/7 food spots, so you can order something anytime.

That “always moving” energy is something I really enjoy about living in HCMC.

So I’d summarize it like this:
HCMC → chaotic but efficient, city that never sleeps
Da Nang → beautiful, slower, and more relaxed
Both are great cities, just very different vibes.

Maybe in the future service in Da Nang will improve, and if you come back you might have a much better experience. 😁

quoted_tweet.text:
Left Da Nang and will probably not come back. 

Spent a total of 5 weeks here. 

I went to bed slightly angry almost every night because of bad service/hospitality, noise, dangerous driving or a mix of those. 

It affected my gf even more so we decided to not stay longer than 1 month.

I think that’s a good proxy for liking a place. Our nervous system just never really felt at ease.

In terms of Vietnam in general, I feel like I had a much better time in HCMC when I stayed there for two weeks a few years ago. 

Everything seemed to be more efficient there and people were much friendlier.

All my Vietnamese friends are super cool, funny and really friendly. 

So I was quite disappointed when I noticed most locals in Da Nang being so cold and borderline unfriendly.

This is the first city in South East Asia this happened to me and if anyone knows why I’d love to learn more about it. 

Maybe it was just us? Maybe locals just don’t like tourists/foreigners? 

No idea but it felt “off”. Almost not welcomed.

The Indiehacker community is really cool and friendly though.

Some cafes are definitely nice to work from Da Nang and the actual coffee is great. Just strong… very strong hehe

The thing with those coffee shops is just that I’m slowly approaching 30 and can’t sit on ultra uncomfortable chairs for an entire day anymore (👴)

When I first arrived I was super stoked because there are not a lot of nomad spots with breezy sunny weather in Jan/Feb and Da Nang definitely has that.

The cons unfortunately outweigh the pros so I’ll likely not come back for the foreseeable future. 

All that being said, if you have a short runway and want to save money it might still be one of the better places to go so I’d say it’s worth giving it a try!

Arrived in Da Nang! 🇻🇳 

I think we arrived with too high expectations 😬 

It honestly feels like Bali but ordered on Wish but in a good way… let me explain.

So after three days here my pros and cons:

Pros:

- ☀️ Amazing weather early in the year

(not too cold not too hot, way better than Bali/BKK/CNX. Think T-Shirt during the day but light wind jacket at night.)

- 💸 Affordable 

(you def. feel it’s much cheaper than most „Nomad“ places but it does come with a cost I‘ll share below)

- 👨🏽‍💻 Community 

(there’s a lot of cool Indiehackers here and you’ll def never feel alone)

- ☕️ Coffee shops 

(this came to a surprise! I’d dare to say the the work-from-a-cafe culture here is the best I have seen from all the places I have been too. Big, spacious, natural light, great coffee, decent WiFi and power plags everywhere)

Now to the cons:

- 🏠 Accommodation 

(this is a personal one but I just can’t seem to find a nice looking apartment or house here for short term rental.

Da Nang seems amazing if you are conscious about your run rate and want basic amenities (think 200-500$ for a basic one bedroom condo)

But if you are used to accommodation from Bali or Bangkok it just doesn’t deliver. 

A good amount of places seem to be riddled with either mold or noise issues. 

We’ve been on countless visits today with various agents, checked all the booking sites and… nada.

There seems to be some nicer high end stuff but it’s all not possible to rent on a monthly basis and seems to avg. $2-4000/m which suddenly doesn’t seem appealing at all anymore given the other options in SEA and beyond.

This is actually also the most frustrating and likely what won’t keep us here for long. 

Still scouting but my initial optimism to find something decent is fading fast.

(I’m sorry to say this but after having driven a lot of vehicles around South East Asia, Vietnam seems to have the worst drivers of all countries I have ever been to with India coming close second)

Initially I thought „oh nice people drive quite slowly here most of time like 40km/h max and there’s no traffic“ so it was refreshing to the traffic craze of Bali but fuak me do people here drive dangerously!

People not only drive on the wrong side of the street (typical SEA behaviour I can handle) but they corner you with acceleration on the wrong side of the street 😅🤯 It’s absolutely nuts. 

We almost had a horrific accident today. My girlfriend cried because it was so sketchy.)

So ye… to summarize Da Nang seems to be THE place if you are starting out your Indiehacker journey and/or want to save money. 

If you care a lot about the quality of your accom or plan to ride a bike while having little to no experience I’m not sure it’s the best place to go.

text:
Da Nang Hotels for Couples: Beach, River, or Quiet Resort

Planning a couple’s stay in Da Nang? Compare My Khe beach hotels, a Han River night, and quieter Son Tra resorts before you book.

Da Nang works for couples who want a beach morning and a city night without changing hotels. The right hotels in Da Nang depend on whether the trip is a swim holiday or a slow weekend.

My Khe is the easy romantic base: sand, a pool, and An Thuong dinners a short walk away. The Han River is better if you want the Dragon Bridge on Saturday or Sunday at 9pm and a quieter morning. Son Tra is the pick when you want fewer bars and a more secluded resort.

Book a room that faces the sea or the river, not the coast road. Ask for a higher floor if the listing sits on Vo Nguyen Giap. A flexible rate still matters — weekend shows and beach weather both move plans.

Compare couple-friendly Da Nang hotels: https://t.co/dDW9OU605n

text:
Cheap Ba Na Hills Tour 2026: A Deeper Guide to Tickets, Timing, and What Actually Saves Money

Ba Na Hills is the most expensive half-day in Da Nang if you treat the gate price as fixed. It is much cheaper if you split the cost into three parts: the cable-car ticket, the transfer, and food. Most “rip-off” reviews are really about the last two.

The standard adult ticket for out-of-province and international visitors is about VND 1,000,000 (roughly USD 38). Children 1–1.4 m and seniors are about VND 800,000. Da Nang residents with local ID pay about VND 650,000. Children under 1 m are free. That ticket already covers the round-trip cable car, the Golden Bridge, French Village, gardens, Linh Ung Pagoda on the hill, and most of Fantasy Park. There is no separate Golden Bridge fee. From 1 January 2026, many cable-car tickets are valid for three consecutive days after first use, with unlimited rides in that window.

On Tripcom, full-day Ba Na Hills + Golden Bridge + French Village tours with hotel pickup often list around USD 42–50, sometimes 15% off a USD 50 rack rate. For one or two people, that package is usually cheaper than a gate ticket plus a private car

Compare cheap Ba Na Hills tours and tickets:
https://t.co/0i4xh9KjAi

What the ticket really includes
Included: cable car, Golden Bridge, French Village, flower gardens, hilltop Linh Ung Pagoda, and the indoor Fantasy Park games hall. Not included, and easy to overspend on: alpine coaster (about VND 70,000–100,000), wax museum, wine cellar, and almost all sit-down food. A standalone lunch buffet on the mountain is often around VND 300,000–380,000. A combo ticket plus buffet can look cheaper than buying both separately, but only if you were going to eat that buffet anyway.

Cheap vs convenient, by group size
1 person: a guided tour with pickup wins. A waiting private car from Da Nang or Hoi An can cost nearly as much as the ticket.
2 people: still often cheaper on a discounted tour than DIY, once you add the return ride.
3–4 people: online tickets plus one shared car usually beat a packaged tour per head.
Da Nang hotel base: check Sun World’s free WOW Bus from central and My Khe stops before you pay for a transfer.

How to get more value from one ticket
Go up on the first cable car. The Golden Bridge is clear, cool, and empty before tour buses arrive; afternoon cloud often hides the valley. If fog kills the photos, the 72-hour validity means a second morning is not a second ticket. Wear a jacket. The summit is often 15–20°C while the beach is hot. Skip a-la-carte snacks on the hill and eat in Da Nang before or after.

A useful cheap-day shape: early cable car, Golden Bridge first, French Village and gardens, Fantasy Park only if the weather turns, cable car down by early afternoon. That uses the expensive part of the ticket and avoids the expensive part of the menu.

Lock a Ba Na Hills day tour or ticket while the discounted rate and free-cancellation slot are still open.

text:
✦ The Itinerary ✦ 

Day 1 – Hanoi Opens Gently

Cyclo Rickshaw Ride → Lotte World Aquarium → Thang Long Water Puppets - the perfect warm-up.

Day 2 – Anniversary on Halong Bay

Comfortable Limousine bus, Breath taking Sung Sot Cave, Ti Top Island, Bamboo boat/kayak in Beautiful Luon Cave lagoons, Veg Indian Meal & cruise rooftop cocktails/hi-tea Dj Party
A day that felt tailored for celebration.
Booked via Klook ₹3,440 + ₹10k (Times Black Voucher)

Day 3 – Hanoi By Sight & Sound

Double-decker tour → Maison Central (can skip) → Train Street nail-biter timing  → Lotte Observation Deck (reflections from screens behind ruined the pics) → Weekend Night market.

Day 4 – Danang Mornings & Fiery Nights

Linh Ung Pagoda — Monkey Mountain Breeze & Coastal Line View. 
Love Pier — Romantic Vibe. 
Han & Son Tra — Bustling Market
Dragon Bridge Fire Show. 
Unreal casual unplanned day spent so well.

Day 5 Ba Na Hills – A Birthday Above the Clouds

A cable car 🚠 ride that felt like a dream.
European architecture & cobbled alleys that felt like Hogwarts. Alpine Coaster 🎢 and the thrilling Fantasy Park. A Golden Bridge 🌉  that lived up to its fame
And a wife who ended her birthday smiling —  mission accomplished 🙂

Day 6  Quick Recap & Hoi An Evenings

Some experiences call you back, and Ba Na Hills did exactly that. We repeated the Alpine Coaster and Fantasy Park rides in the morning and revisited the Golden Bridge, now wrapped in a mystical fog.
The day transitioned into Hoi An with a thrilling basket boat ride, a peaceful walk through the lantern-lit Ancient Town, a serene lantern boat drift, and finally, the spectacular Hoi An Memories Show to close the night.

Day 7 Danang - A Day of Calm & Curiosity

Marble Mountain’s underground caves impressed us, My Khe Beach rested us, and Wonder Park was a chic-click stop for photos. We enjoyed a fun sunset at the resort beach before heading to Vincom Center for shopping. A gentle day of exploration.

Day 8-9 Bangkok in Motion

Asiatique at night was lively and refreshing. The next day, we visited Wat Pho’s reclining Buddha and the Grand Palace glowing golden in the sun. ICONSIAM impressed us with its floating market and indoor waterfall, and we reached the fountain show just in time. Bangkok never disappoints—traffic does—but the city continues to overwhelm in the best ways. We skipped many main attractions this time, as our focus was covering the places we missed on our last trip.

Day 10 Bangkok - The Final Sprint

Platinum Mall, Pratunam Market, Indra Square.  Packing, reflections, and a flight home with bags heavier — minds tired, hearts full...

text:
Our room at Mercure Ba Na Hills was everything we could’ve wished for—beautifully decorated for our anniversary, with a private terrace overlooking the misty hills. The thick fog made it feel surreal, almost like we were floating in a dream.

By evening, the sky began to clear, and wow. We walked to the iconic Golden Bridge, with fewer crowds and a gentle breeze. Truly one of those “you had to be there” moments 🌉✨

At night, Ba Na Hills transforms—quiet, chilly, and magical. Strolling through the fog-covered French village felt like wandering a sleepy European town in the clouds 🌫️

Dinner was back at the hotel, and thanks to Accor Plus, we got the buffet at 50% off—a delicious mix of local and international dishes 🍽️

To end the night, we hit the basement pub—great drinks, upbeat music, and dancing late into the night. A perfect end to a perfect day 💃🥂

text:
Stayed for free at the Mercure in Ba Na Hills, Da nang. The experience was truly different and amazing! Example: They even bring your luggage on the cable car as there is no other transport to go up, which takes 22 minutes long and is the longest in the world.

The weather was so cold and foggy that we could barely see a few feet in front of us. I snapped some pictures of the main circle area, the famous Golden Bridge and my daughter loving to walk, dance everywhere we went in ba na hills due to amazing weather and ambience.

The best part about staying there is that you can go on all the rides and visit the attractions after the general public leaves around 3 or 4 PM. Everything stays open until 7 PM just for hotel guests, so there are no crowds at all. Even golden bridge is open from 6 am to 8 am exclusively for hotel guests hence no crowd ;)

How i got free stay? Thanks to accor points i collected from different credit cards, + they upgraded me to a suite room due to gold member of accor.

Do you want me to post more experiences I had from my recent trip to vietnam?

text:
The Golden Bridge in Da Nang is definitely worth a visit. The weather changes rapidly, sometimes sunny, sometimes cloudy, and sometimes foggy, each bringing a different experience.

The Golden Bridge (Cầu Vàng in Vietnamese) is a famous landmark in Da Nang, Vietnam, located within the Bà Nà Hills tourist resort.

It also serves as a viewing platform, allowing visitors to overlook the surrounding Annamite Mountains and the East Sea.

The Golden Bridge is not just a functional bridge but also a symbol of Vietnam’s tourism industry. Its design is inspired by local Vietnamese folklore, with the giant hands believed to represent mountain gods, holding up the golden bridge as a metaphor for nature’s protection of humanity.

The success of the Golden Bridge also reflects Vietnam’s recent efforts to vigorously develop its tourism industry. According to the vision of Sun Group (the investor behind the Golden Bridge), this bridge has not only elevated the prominence of Bà Nà Hills but also injected new vitality into the tourism industry of Da Nang and Vietnam as a whole. It has been hailed as one of the “Top Ten New Wonders of the World” (based on a poll of young people by the UK’s Daily Mail).

text:
Vietnam Trip: 11 Days for ₹1,00,000 INR (Sep 2025)

Day 1: Delhi to Hanoi - Flight, check-in, coffee, Hoàn Kiếm Lake.
Day 2: Hanoi to Sapa - Limousine, resort, alpine coaster, rent scooter.
Day 3: Sapa - Cable car to Mt. Fansipan, Cat Cat Village, shooting club, Sun Plaza.
Day 4: Sapa - Scooter to Sơn Bình, Glass/Cloud Bridge, Silver Waterfall, markets.
Day 5: Sapa to Hanoi - Train Street, Hoàn Kiếm Lake, street market.
Day 6: Hanoi - Banana Island, Old Quarter, coffee shopping.
Day 7: Hanoi to Da Nang - Flight, Chicland Hotel, My Khe Beach.
Day 8: Da Nang - Pool, parasailing, Sơn Trà Market, Dragon Bridge show.
Day 9: Da Nang - Ba Na Hills, Golden Bridge, beach.
Day 10: Hoi An - Boat ride, markets, old town.
Day 11: Hoi An to Da Nang to Delhi - Flights home.

Expenses: Visa ₹2200, Flights ₹29k, Hotels ₹24k/person, Attractions ₹13.7k, Rest for food/transport (~₹30k + ₹10k emergency).

Tips: Use Grab/Klook, carry USD/zero forex card, 10L VND=₹3400. Add Ninh Binh/Ha Long if desired. 

(Original by sumitkbehal)

text:
🏰 BÀ NÀ HILLS – THE ONLY PLACE WHERE EVEN THE CLOUDS HAVE TO BUY A TICKET! 😂☁️

People ask:
“What’s up at Bà Nà?”

I answer:
* Clouds.
* Castles.
* The Golden Bridge.
* A wine cellar.
* Flower gardens.
* Cable cars.
* And…

…the feeling of visiting for just one day but taking enough photos to post on Facebook until next Tết. 🤣
⸻
You only get it once you’re there…

The clouds here don’t just float overhead; they drift right past your face.

Sometimes you’re striking a cool pose… and a cloud drifts by. Suddenly, your nose vanishes. ☁️🤣
⸻
Even the InterLink mascot standing next to me said seriously:

“This isn’t just a tourist spot…” >>> “It’s nature’s giant studio.”

I looked around… Yeah, it really is.

Every angle looks like a poster. Every spot feels like a movie trailer.
⸻
Passing by the wine cellar…

I thought it was just about wine. But to my surprise…

There’s a “confession walkway” too. ❤️

Couples suddenly start walking slower than public Wi-Fi. As for the singles? Standing there taking photos with the mascot… having just as much fun. 😂
⸻
By the end of the day, I realized…

The most beautiful thing about Bà Nà… isn’t the castle. It isn’t the Golden Bridge.

It’s… the moments spent laughing, forgetting about my phone and deadlines, and remembering that life still holds so many lovely things waiting to be discovered. 💜
⸻
If you ever feel tired…

Don’t try to find a perfect place. Find a place that makes you smile.

Who knows…

That place might just be Bà Nà Hills. ☁️🏰🌸

text:
Real Benefits of Staying Overnight at Accor’s Mercure Ba Na Hills 🏰☁️
Save Time • Save Money • Experience the REAL Ba Na Hills

If Ba Na Hills, Vietnam 🇻🇳 is on your itinerary, do NOT do it as a day trip.
An overnight stay at Mercure Ba Na Hills French Village completely changes the experience — and most people miss this 👇

⸻

🚡 World’s most unique hotel access — arrive by cable car with luggage
This is the ONLY hotel where you reach your hotel room via cable car — with your luggage 🎒🧳
Your stay literally starts with a scenic cable car journey over the lush green forest, waterfalls and through the clouds ☁️
No roads. No buses. Just views and vibes.

⸻

✨ Ba Na Hills at night = pure magic
After sunset 🌄, it feels like you’re staying above the clouds ☁️
Silent streets, misty castles, and unreal vibes — something day visitors never see.

🚶‍♂️ Post 4:30 PM = Ba Na Hills becomes yours
Once the day crowd leaves:
• Empty streets
• Quiet castles
• Peaceful photo spots 📸
• Zero chaos

⸻

🚡 VIP Cable Car access (Huge hidden benefit!)
✔️ Mercure guests get VIP / priority entry into cable cars
✔️ Private cable cars for your family only
✔️ No queues at all

⏳ Day visitors wait 60–90 minutes EACH side, and 10–15 people are packed into one cable car.
This benefit alone saves hours.

⸻

🎢 Fantasy Park with ZERO crowds
🗓️ Friday–Sunday: Open till 7 PM in the evening while day visitors leave by 4:30 PM.
Unlimited FREE Rides, games, and 4D/5D shows — repeated multiple times 🎮🎠
No queues. No rush. Full fun mode 😍

⸻

🎿 Alpine Coaster Happy Hours = Double Win at this Gravity Based Roller Coasters 🎢, Most Popular at Ba Na
💰 Pay just VND 50k (instead of VND 80k)
⏰ 4:30–5:30 PM | 8:30–9:30 AM
🚫 Almost no waiting
🌫️ Evening mist rides on mountains = unforgettable

⸻

🌉 Golden Hand Bridge — crowd-free access
The iconic Golden Bridge is accessible ONLY to Mercure guests from 6 AM–8 AM
Till ~9 AM, there are very few people — perfect for photos & serenity 📸

⸻

🚡 30% discount on Cable Car + ALL attractions if purchased at Mercure check-in, 
The two-way Cable Car tickets includes 👇following on all days on your Stay
✔️ All cable cars (up, down & internal)
✔️ All funiculars 🚆
✔️ Unlimited Fantasy Park & Moon Castle games
✔️ 4D / 5D / 7D & 360° movies
✔️ Flying Eye Theatre
✔️ Indoor & outdoor bumper cars
✔️ All rides
✔️ Sun Castle & Moon/Lunar Castle
✔️ Le Jardin D’Amour, Pagoda & Love Garden 🌸
✔️ Thác Thần Mặt Trời waterfall & Golden Horse Statue
✔️Except Alpine Coasters & 10D Show, everything is Free, unlimited times 🤩

Most day visitors don’t even realise what they miss.

⸻

💡 Bottom Line:
Ba Na Hills is NOT meant to be rushed.
You need time to feel the vibe and explore peacefully.

After staying there, I honestly wished I had booked 2 nights instead of 1.

🏰 A night stay at Mercure Ba Na Hills isn’t just about the hotel — it unlocks the best version of Ba Na Hills.

text:
Day 2 | 14 June 2026

Exploring Ho Chi Minh City

Morning

Breakfast at ibis Saigon Airport.

9:00 AM – Departed from the hotel for the Cu Chi Tunnels.

11:45 AM – Reached Cu Chi Tunnels and explored one of Vietnam’s most iconic historical attractions.

1:00 PM – Visited the Shooting Range and experienced live firearm shooting.

⸻

Afternoon

3:30 PM – Reached Saigon Central Post Office.

Had lunch before heading to the famous Apartment Café.

4:00 PM – Reached Apartment Café.

Enjoyed:

Vietnamese Coffee
Coconut Coffee

Spent some time exploring the cafés and the surrounding streets.

⸻

Evening

5:45 PM – Clicked photographs in front of:

Saigon Central Post Office
Notre-Dame Cathedral Basilica of Saigon

5:55 PM – Visited the Independence Palace.

6:30 PM onwards – Explored Ben Thanh Market, browsing local shops and experiencing the vibrant evening atmosphere.

⸻

Night

Returned to ibis Saigon Airport and had dinner at the hotel.

10:30 PM – Headed out again to explore the Ben Vien Night Street, enjoying the lively nightlife before calling it a day.

text:
Day 3 | 15 June 2026

Ho Chi Minh City → Da Nang → Ba Na Hills

Morning

Had breakfast at ibis Saigon Airport before checking out.

8:30 AM – Left the hotel using the complimentary airport shuttle.

8:45 AM – Reached the airport and completed VietJet check-in.

8:55 AM – Security and boarding formalities were completed within minutes.

Before boarding, relaxed at the Le Saigonnais SASCO Business Lounge.

10:30 AM – Boarded the VietJet Boss Class flight to Da Nang.

12:15 PM – Landed at Da Nang International Airport.

⸻

Afternoon

Travelled by road towards Ba Na Hills.

Heavy rainfall between 2:00 PM and 5:00 PM delayed the gondola operations.

Finally boarded the gondola at 3:45 PM and reached Mercure Danang French Village Bana Hills around 4:30 PM.

⸻

Evening

Spent the evening exploring the beautiful Ba Na Hills and French Village.

Enjoyed:

Alpine Coaster
Bumper Cars

Had dinner at the hotel before taking a leisurely walk around the property and calling it a day.

⸻

Tips from Our Experience

Alpine Coaster tickets are available at discounted prices between 8:00 AM–9:00 AM and 4:00 PM–5:00 PM.
Ba Na Hills becomes much quieter and more enjoyable after 6:00 PM, once the day visitors leave. Staying overnight at the Mercure offers a completely different experience, allowing you to enjoy the attractions and French Village in a peaceful atmosphere.

text:
Day 6: Golden Bridges 🌉 & Da Nang Breezes 🌬️🌴

We woke up early to catch sunrise at Ba Na Hills—and it was pure magic. By 6:30 AM, we were on the cable car, watching clouds drift around the Golden Bridge in soft morning light. Easily one of the trip’s best moments.

After breakfast and checkout, we left our bags at reception and squeezed in some fun—Alpine Coaster rides and lively street performances. Ba Na Hills felt like a European fairytale floating in the clouds.

We collected our bags and took the cable car back down, then headed to Da Nang.

text:
Vietnam 🇻🇳

Bana Hills in Da Nang is an amusement park built on the site of an early 20th century French colonial village. It’s worth visiting here for three reasons: ride the highest cable car in the world, walk along the Golden Bridge and see the French village.

Ba Na Hills is a very atmospheric place and a must visit in Da Nang. You can skip Marble Caves and Michonne, but not going to Ba Na Hills is a crime. In my opinion, Bana Hills Park is one of the best attractions in Vietnam.

text:
📍Ba Na Hills, Da Nang, Vietnam 🇲🇦

By - vietnammoment 🎥

Ba Na Hills is a famous hill station and resort located about 25 km southwest of Da Nang, Vietnam. Situated at an altitude of 1,500 meters, it offers cool weather, scenic views, and a wide range of attractions. Key highlights include the Golden Bridge (held by giant stone hands), the French Village, and the Ba Na cable car—one of the longest in the world. It’s a top tourist destination for both natural beauty and unique architecture.

text: Ba Na Hills a mountain resort located in the Trường Sơn Mountains near Da Nang Vietnam. It's about 25 km west of Da Nang city. Ba Na Hills is known for its cool climate, stunning views and various attractions including a replica of a French medieval town, gardens and amusement parks. The Ba Na Hills Cable Car is a highlight, holding the record for the longest non-stop cable car at over 5,800 meters. It is managed by Sun World and is a popular tourist destination. 🌼💮

𝗕𝗿𝗶𝗱𝗴𝗲𝘀 𝗶𝗻 𝘁𝗵𝗲 Sl8 𝗪𝗮𝗹𝗹𝗲𝘁: $USDC 𝗗𝗲𝗽𝗼𝘀𝗶𝘁𝘀, 𝗦𝘁𝗮𝗸𝗶𝗻𝗴, 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝗥𝗲𝗳𝗲𝗿𝗿𝗮𝗹 𝗥𝗲𝘄𝗮𝗿𝗱𝘀. 𝗣𝗮𝗿𝘁 𝟮

In our previous post https://t.co/FqzfLjUPvr, we introduced 𝗦𝘁𝗮𝗿 𝗚𝗮𝘁𝗲 𝗕𝗿𝗶𝗱𝗴𝗲 - 𝗮 𝗳𝗲𝗮𝘁𝘂𝗿𝗲 𝗯𝘂𝗶𝗹𝘁 𝗶𝗻𝘁𝗼 𝘁𝗵𝗲 Sl8 𝘄𝗮𝗹𝗹𝗲𝘁 and explained how to deposit cryptocurrency from different blockchains and receive the corresponding tokens from our 𝟭𝟬 𝗮𝘃𝗮𝗶𝗹𝗮𝗯𝗹𝗲 𝘀𝗴-𝗮𝘀𝘀𝗲𝘁𝘀:
• sgXRP - $XRP: via XRP Ledger.
• sgRLUSD - $RLUSD: via XRP Ledger.
• sgSOL - $SOL: via Solana.
• sgTRX - $TRX: via TRON.
• sgUSDT - $USDT: via Avalanche C-Chain, Ethereum, Solana, TON using the Jetton standard, and TRON using the TRC-20 standard.
• sgBNB - $BNB: via BNB Chain.
• sgPOL - $POL: via Polygon.
• sgETH - $ETH: via Ethereum and Optimism.
• sgTON - $TON ($GRAM): via the TON network.
• sgAVAX - $AVAX: via Avalanche C-Chain.

Now, let’s continue exploring our wallet and focus on $USDC - 𝗼𝗻𝗲 𝗼𝗳 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗺𝗮𝗶𝗻 𝗮𝘀𝘀𝗲𝘁𝘀 𝘂𝘀𝗲𝗱 𝗳𝗼𝗿 𝗽𝗮𝘆𝗺𝗲𝗻𝘁𝘀 𝗼𝗻 Sl8.
With $USDC, you can 𝗽𝘂𝗿𝗰𝗵𝗮𝘀𝗲 𝗮𝗰𝗰𝗲𝘀𝘀 𝘁𝗼 𝗽𝗮𝗶𝗱 𝗽𝗼𝘀𝘁𝘀 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝗼𝘁𝗵𝗲𝗿 𝗰𝗼𝗻𝘁𝗲𝗻𝘁, 𝗽𝗮𝘆 𝗳𝗼𝗿 𝘀𝘂𝗯𝘀𝗰𝗿𝗶𝗽𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻𝘀, 𝘀𝗲𝗻𝗱 𝘁𝗶𝗽𝘀, 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝘀𝘂𝗽𝗽𝗼𝗿𝘁 𝗰𝗿𝗲𝗮𝘁𝗼𝗿𝘀 𝘄𝗶𝘁𝗵 𝘀𝗽𝗲𝗰𝗶𝗮𝗹 𝗹𝗶𝗸𝗲𝘀. Special likes also support $SSLX, the platform’s token, so you choose which asset to use when supporting a post.
$USDC is also used for 𝘁𝗿𝗮𝗻𝘀𝗳𝗲𝗿𝘀, 𝘀𝘄𝗮𝗽𝘀 𝗶𝗻𝘁𝗼 𝘀𝘂𝗽𝗽𝗼𝗿𝘁𝗲𝗱 𝘁𝗼𝗸𝗲𝗻𝘀, 𝗽𝗮𝗿𝘁𝗶𝗰𝗶𝗽𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻 𝗶𝗻 𝗹𝗶𝗾𝘂𝗶𝗱𝗶𝘁𝘆 𝗽𝗼𝗼𝗹𝘀, 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝘀𝘁𝗮𝗸𝗶𝗻𝗴. Payouts of available rewards through the 𝗣𝗮𝘆𝗼𝘂𝘁 section are also made in $USDC.
In this post, we’ll focus on 𝗳𝘂𝗻𝗱𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝘆𝗼𝘂𝗿 𝘄𝗮𝗹𝗹𝗲𝘁 𝗳𝗿𝗼𝗺 𝗱𝗶𝗳𝗳𝗲𝗿𝗲𝗻𝘁 𝗻𝗲𝘁𝘄𝗼𝗿𝗸𝘀, 𝘀𝘁𝗮𝗸𝗶𝗻𝗴 $USDC, 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗿𝗲𝗳𝗲𝗿𝗿𝗮𝗹 𝗽𝗿𝗼𝗴𝗿𝗮𝗺, 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝘄𝗶𝘁𝗵𝗱𝗿𝗮𝘄𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗳𝘂𝗻𝗱𝘀. We’ll explore other ways to use $USDC in more detail in future posts.
Importantly, 𝗦𝘁𝗮𝗿 𝗚𝗮𝘁𝗲 𝗕𝗿𝗶𝗱𝗴𝗲 𝗽𝗿𝗼𝘃𝗶𝗱𝗲𝘀 𝗮𝗻 𝗮𝗱𝗱𝗶𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻𝗮𝗹 𝘄𝗮𝘆 𝘁𝗼 𝗳𝘂𝗻𝗱 𝘆𝗼𝘂𝗿 𝘄𝗮𝗹𝗹𝗲𝘁 𝗳𝗿𝗼𝗺 𝗼𝘁𝗵𝗲𝗿 𝗯𝗹𝗼𝗰𝗸𝗰𝗵𝗮𝗶𝗻𝘀. Direct deposits through the 𝗦𝘁𝗲𝗹𝗹𝗮𝗿 network continue to work as usual. You can still send supported Stellar assets, including $USDC 𝗮𝗻𝗱 $XLM, using the deposit details under 𝗧𝗼𝗽𝘂𝗽 → 𝗦𝘁𝗲𝗹𝗹𝗮𝗿.
If your $USDC is on another supported network, follow the deposit process below.

𝗛𝗼𝘄 𝘁𝗼 𝗱𝗲𝗽𝗼𝘀𝗶𝘁 $USDC 𝗳𝗿𝗼𝗺 𝗮𝗻𝗼𝘁𝗵𝗲𝗿 𝗯𝗹𝗼𝗰𝗸𝗰𝗵𝗮𝗶𝗻
In your Sl8 wallet, open 𝗪𝗮𝗹𝗹𝗲𝘁 → 𝗧𝗼𝗽𝘂𝗽 → 𝗚𝗮𝘁𝗲 𝗮𝘀𝘀𝗲𝘁𝘀 → 𝗨𝗦𝗗𝗖.
𝗦𝗲𝘃𝗲𝗻 𝗻𝗲𝘁𝘄𝗼𝗿𝗸𝘀 are currently available:
• 𝗔𝗿𝗰
• 𝗔𝘃𝗮𝗹𝗮𝗻𝗰𝗵𝗲 𝗖-𝗖𝗵𝗮𝗶𝗻
• 𝗕𝗮𝘀𝗲
• 𝗘𝘁𝗵𝗲𝗿𝗲𝘂𝗺
• 𝗢𝗽𝘁𝗶𝗺𝗶𝘀𝗺
• 𝗣𝗼𝗹𝘆𝗴𝗼𝗻
• 𝗦𝗼𝗹𝗮𝗻𝗮

Select the network where your $USDC is held. We’ll then display the 𝗱𝗲𝗽𝗼𝘀𝗶𝘁 𝗮𝗱𝗱𝗿𝗲𝘀𝘀, 𝗤𝗥 𝗰𝗼𝗱𝗲, 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝗰𝘂𝗿𝗿𝗲𝗻𝘁 𝗹𝗶𝗺𝗶𝘁𝘀 for that route.

𝗙𝗼𝗿 𝘁𝗵𝗶𝘀 $USDC 𝗱𝗲𝗽𝗼𝘀𝗶𝘁 𝗺𝗲𝘁𝗵𝗼𝗱, 𝘆𝗼𝘂 𝗿𝗲𝗰𝗲𝗶𝘃𝗲 𝗮 𝗽𝗲𝗿𝘀𝗼𝗻𝗮𝗹 𝗱𝗲𝗽𝗼𝘀𝗶𝘁 𝗮𝗱𝗱𝗿𝗲𝘀𝘀, 𝘀𝗼 𝗻𝗼 𝗠𝗘𝗠𝗢 𝗶𝘀 𝗿𝗲𝗾𝘂𝗶𝗿𝗲𝗱.

Copy the address into the external wallet or exchange you’ll be sending from. Select 𝗨𝗦𝗗𝗖, enter the amount, and check the details before confirming.

𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝘀𝗲𝗻𝗱𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗻𝗲𝘁𝘄𝗼𝗿𝗸 𝗺𝘂𝘀𝘁 𝗺𝗮𝘁𝗰𝗵 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗻𝗲𝘁𝘄𝗼𝗿𝗸 𝘀𝗲𝗹𝗲𝗰𝘁𝗲𝗱 𝗶𝗻 Sl8. For example, if you opened deposit details for Solana, send your $USDC through Solana.

Check the minimum and maximum amounts for your selected route: 𝗹𝗶𝗺𝗶𝘁𝘀 𝗺𝗮𝘆 𝘃𝗮𝗿𝘆 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝗰𝗵𝗮𝗻𝗴𝗲 𝗼𝘃𝗲𝗿 𝘁𝗶𝗺𝗲.

Also account for any fee charged by the service you’re sending from. If it deducts the fee from your transfer amount, fewer tokens will reach the address than you entered. The actual amount received must meet the deposit limits.

𝗗𝗲𝗽𝗼𝘀𝗶𝘁𝘀 𝗯𝗲𝗹𝗼𝘄 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗺𝗶𝗻𝗶𝗺𝘂𝗺 𝗮𝗿𝗲 𝗻𝗼𝘁 𝗰𝗿𝗲𝗱𝗶𝘁𝗲𝗱 𝗮𝘂𝘁𝗼𝗺𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗰𝗮𝗹𝗹𝘆 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝗿𝗲𝗾𝘂𝗶𝗿𝗲 𝗰𝗼𝗻𝘁𝗮𝗰𝘁𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝘀𝘂𝗽𝗽𝗼𝗿𝘁.

Once the transfer has been processed, we’ll credit $USDC 𝗼𝗻 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗦𝘁𝗲𝗹𝗹𝗮𝗿 𝗻𝗲𝘁𝘄𝗼𝗿𝗸 𝗮𝘁 𝗮 𝟭:𝟭 𝗿𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼. This ratio refers to the number of tokens; any costs of sending the transfer are accounted for separately.

You can check the transaction status using 𝗧𝗿𝗮𝗰𝗸 𝘁𝗵𝗶𝘀 𝗱𝗲𝗽𝗼𝘀𝗶𝘁 and your transaction history.

Copy the address into the external wallet or exchange you’ll be sending from. Select 𝗨𝗦𝗗𝗖, enter the amount, and check the details before confirming.

Also account for any fee charged by the service you’re sending from. If it deducts the fee from your transfer amount, fewer tokens will reach the address than you entered. The actual amount received must meet the deposit limits.

𝗗𝗲𝗽𝗼𝘀𝗶𝘁𝘀 𝗯𝗲𝗹𝗼𝘄 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗺𝗶𝗻𝗶𝗺𝘂𝗺 𝗮𝗿𝗲 𝗻𝗼𝘁 𝗰𝗿𝗲𝗱𝗶𝘁𝗲𝗱 𝗮𝘂𝘁𝗼𝗺𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗰𝗮𝗹𝗹𝘆 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝗿𝗲𝗾𝘂𝗶𝗿𝗲 𝗰𝗼𝗻𝘁𝗮𝗰𝘁𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝘀𝘂𝗽𝗽𝗼𝗿𝘁.

Once the transfer has been processed, we’ll credit $USDC 𝗼𝗻 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗦𝘁𝗲𝗹𝗹𝗮𝗿 𝗻𝗲𝘁𝘄𝗼𝗿𝗸 𝗮𝘁 𝗮 𝟭:𝟭 𝗿𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼. This ratio refers to the number of tokens; any costs of sending the transfer are accounted for separately.

You can check the transaction status using 𝗧𝗿𝗮𝗰𝗸 𝘁𝗵𝗶𝘀 𝗱𝗲𝗽𝗼𝘀𝗶𝘁 and your transaction history.
Once credited, the funds will appear in your 𝗔𝘀𝘀𝗲𝘁𝘀 list. Depositing adds funds to your balance. To participate in staking, you need to select and confirm a plan separately.
𝗛𝗼𝘄 𝘁𝗼 𝘀𝘁𝗮𝗸𝗲 $USDC
Open 𝗨𝗦𝗗𝗖 in your asset list and select 𝗦𝘁𝗮𝗸𝗲.
𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝗺𝗶𝗻𝗶𝗺𝘂𝗺 𝘀𝘁𝗮𝗸𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗮𝗺𝗼𝘂𝗻𝘁 𝗶𝘀 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗲𝗾𝘂𝗶𝘃𝗮𝗹𝗲𝗻𝘁 𝗼𝗳 $100 𝗶𝗻 $USDC. This threshold applies specifically to staking and is separate from the wallet’s deposit limits.
You choose your staking period:
• 𝟯𝟬 𝗱𝗮𝘆𝘀

Your staking plan will show the 𝗔𝗣𝗬 𝗿𝗮𝘁𝗲 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝗲𝘀𝘁𝗶𝗺𝗮𝘁𝗲𝗱 𝗿𝗲𝘄𝗮𝗿𝗱 𝗮𝘁 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗲𝗻𝗱 𝗼𝗳 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝘁𝗲𝗿𝗺.

APY stands for annual percentage yield. It does not mean you receive the full annual percentage over 30 or 90 days. To assess the result for your chosen term, refer to the reward estimate shown in the plan.

𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝗔𝗣𝗬 𝗿𝗮𝘁𝗲 𝗶𝘀 𝗳𝗶𝘅𝗲𝗱 𝘄𝗵𝗲𝗻 𝘆𝗼𝘂 𝘀𝘁𝗮𝗸𝗲. 𝗥𝗲𝘄𝗮𝗿𝗱𝘀 𝗳𝗼𝗿 𝘀𝘁𝗮𝗸𝗶𝗻𝗴 $USDC 𝗮𝗿𝗲 𝗽𝗮𝗶𝗱 𝗶𝗻 $USDC.

Before confirming, check the amount, term, estimated reward, and automatic renewal settings.

𝗘𝗮𝗿𝗹𝘆 𝘂𝗻𝘀𝘁𝗮𝗸𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗶𝘀 𝗻𝗼𝘁 𝗮𝘃𝗮𝗶𝗹𝗮𝗯𝗹𝗲. Staked funds cannot be transferred or withdrawn before the plan ends. Choose an amount and term that account for when you may need access to those funds.

Automatic renewal is enabled 𝗮𝘁 𝘆𝗼𝘂𝗿 𝗱𝗶𝘀𝗰𝗿𝗲𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻. If it is disabled, once the term ends, 𝘆𝗼𝘂𝗿 𝘀𝘁𝗮𝗸𝗲𝗱 𝗽𝗿𝗶𝗻𝗰𝗶𝗽𝗮𝗹 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝗿𝗲𝘄𝗮𝗿𝗱 𝘄𝗶𝗹𝗹 𝗯𝗲 𝗿𝗲𝘁𝘂𝗿𝗻𝗲𝗱 𝗱𝗶𝗿𝗲𝗰𝘁𝗹𝘆 𝘁𝗼 𝘆𝗼𝘂𝗿 𝘄𝗮𝗹𝗹𝗲𝘁 𝗶𝗻 $USDC.

You can view information about your active plan in the 𝗦𝘁𝗮𝗸𝗶𝗻𝗴 section.

In addition to rewards from your own stake, Sl8 lets you earn referral rewards from staking by participants in your referral network.

𝗪𝗵𝗮𝘁 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗿𝗲𝗳𝗲𝗿𝗿𝗮𝗹 𝗽𝗿𝗼𝗴𝗿𝗮𝗺 𝗼𝗳𝗳𝗲𝗿𝘀

By inviting users to Sl8, you can earn rewards from their participation in staking. The program extends through 𝘀𝗶𝘅 𝗹𝗲𝘃𝗲𝗹𝘀.

The first level consists of users you invite directly. The second consists of users they invite. This structure continues in the same way through the sixth level.

Your reward is calculated 𝗳𝗿𝗼𝗺 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗮𝗺𝗼𝘂𝗻𝘁 𝘀𝘁𝗮𝗸𝗲𝗱 𝗯𝘆 𝗮 𝗽𝗮𝗿𝘁𝗶𝗰𝗶𝗽𝗮𝗻𝘁 𝗮𝘁 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗰𝗼𝗿𝗿𝗲𝘀𝗽𝗼𝗻𝗱𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗹𝗲𝘃𝗲𝗹:

• 𝗟𝗲𝘃𝗲𝗹 𝟭 - 𝟲%
• 𝗟𝗲𝘃𝗲𝗹 𝟮 - 𝟱%

𝗥𝗲𝗳𝗲𝗿𝗿𝗮𝗹 𝗿𝗲𝘄𝗮𝗿𝗱𝘀 𝗮𝗿𝗲 𝗽𝗮𝗶𝗱 𝗯𝘆 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗽𝗿𝗼𝗷𝗲𝗰𝘁 𝗳𝗿𝗼𝗺 𝗶𝘁𝘀 𝗼𝘄𝗻 𝗳𝘂𝗻𝗱𝘀. The referred user does not pay for them: we do not deduct these amounts from their staked principal or rewards. They receive their funds and full staking reward according to their chosen plan’s terms.

Referral rewards are credited to the 𝗣𝗮𝘆𝗼𝘂𝘁 section. We’ll explain how this section works and how to receive other rewards in a separate post.
𝗛𝗼𝘄 𝘁𝗼 𝘄𝗶𝘁𝗵𝗱𝗿𝗮𝘄 $USDC
Once funds are available in your balance, open 𝗨𝗦𝗗𝗖 in your asset list and select 𝗪𝗶𝘁𝗵𝗱𝗿𝗮𝘄.
Withdrawals support 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝘀𝗮𝗺𝗲 𝘀𝗲𝘃𝗲𝗻 𝗻𝗲𝘁𝘄𝗼𝗿𝗸𝘀 listed in the deposit section. You can choose any of them, regardless of which network you originally used to deposit.

Select the receiving network and paste the recipient’s address.

If you’re sending $USDC to an exchange, copy the address from its 𝗨𝗦𝗗𝗖 𝗱𝗲𝗽𝗼𝘀𝗶𝘁 𝘀𝗲𝗰𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻 𝗳𝗼𝗿 𝘁𝗵𝗮𝘁 𝘀𝗽𝗲𝗰𝗶𝗳𝗶𝗰 𝗻𝗲𝘁𝘄𝗼𝗿𝗸. Make sure the recipient supports this asset on the selected blockchain.

For withdrawals, use 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗿𝗲𝗰𝗶𝗽𝗶𝗲𝗻𝘁’𝘀 𝗱𝗲𝗽𝗼𝘀𝗶𝘁 𝗱𝗲𝘁𝗮𝗶𝗹𝘀, rather than the address we provided for funding your Sl8 wallet.

Select 𝗡𝗲𝘅𝘁 and enter the amount.

𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝘄𝗶𝘁𝗵𝗱𝗿𝗮𝘄𝗮𝗹 𝗳𝗲𝗲 𝗶𝘀 𝟬.𝟱 𝗨𝗦𝗗𝗖 𝗽𝗲𝗿 𝘁𝗿𝗮𝗻𝘀𝗮𝗰𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻. Two fee payment options are available:

• 𝗗𝗲𝗱𝘂𝗰𝘁 𝗳𝗿𝗼𝗺 𝗮𝗺𝗼𝘂𝗻𝘁. If you enter 10 USDC, 10 USDC will be deducted from your balance, and the recipient will receive 9.5 USDC.
• 𝗔𝗱𝗱 𝗼𝗻 𝘁𝗼𝗽. If you enter 10 USDC as the amount to receive, 10.5 USDC will be deducted from your balance.

To add the fee on top, your balance must cover 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝘁𝗿𝗮𝗻𝘀𝗳𝗲𝗿 𝗮𝗺𝗼𝘂𝗻𝘁 𝗽𝗹𝘂𝘀 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗳𝗲𝗲. Check the current limits for your selected route.

At the final step, we’ll display the 𝗻𝗲𝘁𝘄𝗼𝗿𝗸, 𝗿𝗲𝗰𝗶𝗽𝗶𝗲𝗻𝘁 𝗮𝗱𝗱𝗿𝗲𝘀𝘀, 𝘁𝗼𝘁𝗮𝗹 𝗮𝗺𝗼𝘂𝗻𝘁 𝘁𝗼 𝗯𝗲 𝗱𝗲𝗱𝘂𝗰𝘁𝗲𝗱, 𝗳𝗲𝗲, 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝗮𝗺𝗼𝘂𝗻𝘁 𝘁𝗼 𝗯𝗲 𝗿𝗲𝗰𝗲𝗶𝘃𝗲𝗱.

Review this information carefully. If you notice an error, return to the previous step and correct it. Once you’ve checked everything, select 𝗖𝗼𝗻𝗳𝗶𝗿𝗺 𝘄𝗶𝘁𝗵𝗱𝗿𝗮𝘄𝗮𝗹.

Processing usually takes a few minutes. The actual time depends on transaction processing and the destination network. When sending to an exchange, crediting also depends on its rules and required number of confirmations.

𝗪𝗲’𝗿𝗲 𝗰𝗼𝗻𝘁𝗶𝗻𝘂𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝘁𝗼 𝗲𝘅𝗽𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗮𝘃𝗮𝗶𝗹𝗮𝗯𝗹𝗲 𝗻𝗲𝘁𝘄𝗼𝗿𝗸𝘀

For $USDC, we plan to add 𝗔𝗿𝗯𝗶𝘁𝗿𝘂𝗺, 𝗛𝘆𝗽𝗲𝗿𝗹𝗶𝗾𝘂𝗶𝗱, 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝗫𝗥𝗣 𝗟𝗲𝗱𝗴𝗲𝗿. These routes are currently marked as upcoming and are not yet available. We’ll announce their launch and terms of use separately.

𝗕𝗿𝗶𝗱𝗴𝗲𝘀 𝗶𝗻 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗦𝗹𝟴 𝗪𝗮𝗹𝗹𝗲𝘁: 𝘀𝗴 𝗧𝗼𝗸𝗲𝗻𝘀 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝗛𝗼𝘄 𝘁𝗼 𝗨𝘀𝗲 𝗧𝗵𝗲𝗺. 𝗣𝗮𝗿𝘁 𝟭
Across two posts, we’ll explain the bridges built into our wallet and how you can use them. In this first part, we’ll cover how sg tokens work, how to fund your wallet from different networks, stake your funds, and withdraw them.

As you may have already heard, we’ve added 𝗦𝘁𝗮𝗿 𝗚𝗮𝘁𝗲 𝗕𝗿𝗶𝗱𝗴𝗲 to the Sl8 wallet - a feature for depositing and withdrawing cryptocurrencies across different blockchains. You can now deposit a supported asset, use it for staking, and then withdraw it to an external wallet.

For example, if you hold $XRP and want to keep holding that asset, you don’t need to sell it for $USDT or $USDC before participating in staking on Sl8. You deposit $XRP through XRP Ledger, receive sgXRP in our wallet, and choose a suitable staking period.

Let’s walk through how it works.

𝗪𝗵𝗮𝘁 𝗔𝗿𝗲 𝘀𝗴 𝗧𝗼𝗸𝗲𝗻𝘀?
Our wallet operates on the Stellar network. When you use the wallet’s 𝗦𝘁𝗮𝗿 𝗚𝗮𝘁𝗲 𝗕𝗿𝗶𝗱𝗴𝗲 feature to deposit cryptocurrency, we credit the corresponding token with the sg prefix. It represents the underlying asset within Sl8.

𝗘𝗮𝗰𝗵 𝘀𝗴 𝘁𝗼𝗸𝗲𝗻 𝗶𝘀 𝗯𝗮𝗰𝗸𝗲𝗱 𝟭:𝟭 𝗯𝘆 𝗶𝘁𝘀 𝗰𝗼𝗿𝗿𝗲𝘀𝗽𝗼𝗻𝗱𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗰𝗿𝘆𝗽𝘁𝗼𝗰𝘂𝗿𝗿𝗲𝗻𝗰𝘆. For example, each sgXRP is backed by one $XRP. When you withdraw through a selected route, you receive the underlying cryptocurrency, with the transaction fee taken into account.

This ratio refers to the number of tokens. The dollar value of market-priced assets continues to fluctuate: when the price of $XRP changes, the dollar value of sgXRP changes as well.

Once the deposit has been credited, open the relevant sg token in your asset list and select 𝗦𝘁𝗮𝗸𝗲.
